operators.name: reflection_pad2d_forward
semantics: Corresponds to torch.nn.functional.pad with mode='reflect' (ReflectionPad2d) on a 4D input
Padding is symmetric: padding is a single int added to all four spatial sides; reference input padding is 1
Output height = input.height + 2*padding, width = input.width + 2*padding
Reflection padding copies edge values mirrored without repeating the edge pixel; for pad=1, output[:, :, 1:-1, 1:-1] = input and border pixels are reflected from adjacent rows/cols
Preserves dtype float32 and device CUDA; output is a new contiguous tensor

operators.name: count_nonzero_forward

parameters.name: input
parameters.shape: [N, C, H, W] or any shape

semantics: Corresponds to torch.count_nonzero(input) which returns the total number of non-zero elements across all dimensions
Scalar tensor of dtype int64 on CUDA
Counts elements with value != 0, including negative values and NaN
Reduction over all elements, no axes specified

operators.name: upsample_bilinear2d_forward
semantics: Corresponds to nn.Upsample with mode='bilinear', align_corners=False (default for bilinear in PyTorch)
scale_factor is provided as a float (2.0 in this task)
Output height = floor(input.height * scale_factor) = input.height*2 for integer factor, same for width
Bilinear interpolation uses PyTorch's coordinate mapping: src = (dst + 0.5) / scale_factor - 0.5 for align_corners=False
Values at borders are computed with edge clamping; no extrapolation
Preserves dtype float32 and device CUDA; output is a new contiguous tensor
Applies ReflectionPad2d with padding (1,1,1,1) on input [8,3,1024,1024] to produce [8,3,1026,1026]
All spatial borders are padded by reflecting each row/column inward by one pixel
Counts number of non-zero elements in the padded tensor [8,3,1026,1026]
Returns scalar int64 tensor on CUDA
Upsamples padded tensor from [8,3,1026,1026] to [8,3,2052,2052] using bilinear interpolation scale_factor=2.0
Uses align_corners=False as in the reference model
Returns a tuple containing the scalar count tensor and the upscaled float32 tensor
Order and types match reference: (int64 scalar, float32 tensor)
